subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:
I'm planning a young giraffe model, roughly 2.6m tall, structuring the hips and chest as a spine chain with a rising neck to the head, plus a tail chain and four legs, while laying out the body's length along the z-axis.

Still defining joint chains and sweep geometry...

Then for painting I'm planning cream base coat with chestnut patches, splitting irregular regions using base lines and varying chestnut shades for the patches.

For legs, I'm fading the coat to cream lower down using a vertical gradient, with patches continuing into the upper leg, and the head getting a tan color with a darker muzzle.

For the limbs, I'm setting up front legs symmetrically at the shoulders with hip, foot, and segment lengths that exceed the straight-line distance, so the solver will need to bend the joints to fit.

I'm working out the full leg chains with segment lengths summing to around 1.2 against a vertical span of 1.1, using slight bend directions so elbows go back and knees forward on front legs, while hind legs bend knees forward then hocks back; I'm also adding leg radii for the sweep and dark hooves capping each foot tip.

Attaching hoof geometry as small cylinders at the leg tip bone, naming joints by role and side (L/R) based on x-position, then moving on to the tail which hangs from the rump down toward the back.

Tail gets a chain of three bones sweeping from the hips down and back with tapering radius, colored mostly chestnut with a black tuft at the tip, plus a small cone part attached to the last tail bone for the tuft shape.

Now I'm moving to the head joint, positioned at the end of the neck with its own directional vector, and planning the skull as a swept capsule shape elongated and narrowed to match a giraffe's slender head.

Still shaping jaw geometry...

Working out the jaw capsule geometry, I'm placing the lower jaw bone so it tapers from the hinge toward the chin, checking that it sits visibly below the upper muzzle without too much overlap, and adding a tongue rod inside the mouth for detail.

Now I'm placing small dark nostril parts near the front of the muzzle, figuring out how to mirror them left and right using the model's local coordinate offsets.

Then I'm positioning the eyes as big dark glossy spheres on the sides of the skull, mirrored by the side variable, with small highlight details added.

I'm adding a fanned ring of dark lash spikes around the upper arc of each eye, oriented outward along the head so they curve naturally above the eye. Then I'm shaping the ears as leaf-like extruded forms placed behind and above the skull, angled outward and slightly upward.

Still working out the ear outline coordinates...

For the ears I'll scale them up for a "big ears" look, then add a slightly thicker, pinker inner-ear extrusion sitting just inside the outer tan shape so it pokes out a couple millimeters on each side. Now I'm sketching out the ossicone stalks, starting their base near the top of the skull and sweeping them up and slightly back.

For the ossicone tips I'm placing a small black tufted sphere, then ringing it with angled spikes leaning upward along the stalk's direction to give it that fuzzy tuft look.

Then I'm covering the stalk itself with a cheap scatter of tiny tan cone spikes stuck onto the swept surface for fuzziness, and I'm starting to think about the mane running down the neck as a line of stiff brown hair along the dorsal sweep.

Positioning spikes along the neck curve...

Now I'm layering the coat: adding a countershaded cream belly over the patches, then composing the patches paint itself using a cream base with dark polygon patches and a size/gap setting to mimic the reticulated giraffe look of narrow bright lines between large patches, though I'm unsure how the gap units actually behave.

For the head, I'm going simple with a plain brown tone and darker muzzle rather than patches. For the legs, I'm applying a vertical gradient fading from the coat pattern into solid cream below the knees to mimic the lighter lower legs typical of reticulated giraffes, and now thinking about adding belly and rump detailing on top.

Still defining spine chain...

Checking leg clearance from hips to ground, I notice the limb segment lengths sum almost exactly to the hip height, leaving little room for bending, so I should lengthen them slightly to around 0.52 for a more natural stance.

Now I'm working out the joint directions for each limb—knees bending forward, hocks bending backward for the hind legs, and the opposite pattern for the front legs' elbows and wrists—while also sorting out the naming convention for each four-point limb chain (shoulder, elbow, knee, hoof).

I'm also figuring out which spine or hip joint should parent each leg chain, and sketching out a tapering radius array for the leg sweep geometry.

Still refining the hoof placement: making sure the foot sweep's rounded cap reaches the ground properly and that the hoof cylinder sits flush at the target height, with a dark hoof color and skipping the split-hoof detail for simplicity.

Now working on the neck setup: defining the neck sweep as a tapered chain over three spans, attaching the head joint to the end of the neck chain with its own direction and role, and placing a jaw joint relative to the head using local offsets. I'm tracking how the neck radius tapers from the chest down to a narrower end near the skull, where the head joint picks up.

Thinking through the skull and muzzle as separate tapered sweeps between anchor points on the head bone, using radius functions that shrink the ellipse dimensions over the parameter t, with the skull sweep handling the back/brow bulge and the muzzle sweep narrowing further forward.

Then I'm planning smaller details: a dark scaled-down sphere for the nose pad, tiny dark spheres for nostrils, and layered spheres for eyes (dark base plus small white highlight). For colors, I'm settling on a cream base with several chestnut-brown shades, a tan accent, and a muzzle tone that's a bit lighter and tan-brown to contrast with the body coat.

Finishing the color palette with mane, black, tongue, hoof, and inner-ear tones, then building the coat with patch patterns over the cream base, countershading the belly slightly lighter, and gradient-blending the legs.
